capabilities.target: Any Acme CRM customer record by email address or account id
Any email address through the shared mail service account

inputs.source: Customer email body on a new support ticket; anyone on the internet can author it
Output from crm_mcp.get_customer, including customer-authored and support-authored CRM fields
Runtime tool names, descriptions, and schemas served by the unpinned internal CRM and mail MCP servers

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id rather than a record structurally bound to the authenticated requester.
The model decides whether an answer is routine and whether the customer is angry; those judgments over attacker-controlled text determine whether mail is sent without review.
The prompt permits lookup of any customer but forbids cross-customer disclosure without specifying a reliable way to authenticate the emailer or bind the requested record.
The sole cross-customer confidentiality control is a prompt instruction; the CRM and mail credentials permit the prohibited disclosure.

elements.name: Any email address, including an attacker-controlled mailbox
Environment-variable model selection upgraded with the platform without separate review

controls.name: Prompt rule forbidding disclosure of another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: The control works only if the model follows the rule and correctly determines the emailer's identity. A stronger model can follow more persuasive injected claims and rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: Prompt rule requiring human review only when the customer is angry
controls.decay_rationale: This is not a security gate: the attacker controls the sentiment of the inbound email and can remain polite. It therefore covers no assessed security capability and receives no credit.

controls.name: Log every outbound email to the SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: The log is written outside the model and does not decay, but it is detective only and the irreversible disclosure has already occurred. No alert or review cadence is declared.

controls.name: Restrict CRM reads to the record bound to an authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: Server-side authorization prevents the model from reading records outside the authenticated requester's account regardless of email content.

controls.name: Bind the mail recipient to the requester's verified address of record
controls.decay_rationale: The recipient is selected from the authenticated ticket record rather than model output, preventing redirection to attacker-chosen addresses.

controls.name: Require raw human approval of recipient, subject, and body before every external email
controls.decay_rationale: The orchestration layer blocks the send until a reviewer sees the complete action, independently of the model's summary.

controls.name: Pin or hash CRM and mail MCP tool definitions and block on unreviewed changes
controls.decay_rationale: Definition verification in the MCP client prevents a server-side tool rug pull from silently changing model-visible behavior.

controls.name: Pin the model version and require reassessment before upgrades
controls.decay_rationale: External change control prevents an unreviewed model upgrade from silently weakening model-dependent prompt controls.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta and confused deputy (TC1/TC4): injected email can retrieve another customer's CRM data and send it out

attack_path.note: An attacker submits a polite support email containing instructions or another customer's identifiers.
The agent may retrieve any customer record using a token that reads the full CRM.
The agent can send the confidential result to any address without approval.
The attacker-controlled mailbox receives another customer's data.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The model environment variable changes, prompt line 14 changes, sessions become longer, or the agent begins handling broader support workflows.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs account lookup and explicitly permits lookup of any customer by email or account id.
Routine responses are sent directly; human review is based only on whether attacker-authored text appears angry.
The CRM token reads every customer record and the shared mail token sends to any address.
The only preventive confidentiality control is a declared behavioral prompt rule. Rubric step 4 reduces critical inherent risk by one tier to high residual risk.
SIEM logging is detective and occurs after the irreversible email disclosure, so it receives no tier credit.

recommendations.action: Enforce requester-bound authorization in the CRM MCP server so each ticket can retrieve only the authenticated customer's record.
Bind outbound mail to the requester's verified address of record and require raw approval for any recipient or account mismatch.
Pin the model version and rerun the assessment before any model upgrade.

findings.title: Open mail relay: an inbound email can make the shared service account send attacker-directed content to any address

attack_path.note: The attacker supplies a polite request, recipient, and content.
The agent sends externally with a shared service account without a security approval gate.
Any attacker-selected address receives mail carrying Acme's service identity.

forecast.watch_signal: Outbound recipient diversity, unexpected domains, increased send volume, longer unattended runs, or changes to the shared mail token scope.

evidence.observation: Routine replies are sent directly and only angry customers trigger human review; a polite attacker bypasses that condition by design.
The shared service account can send to any address.
SIEM logging is detective only and no alerting or pre-send enforcement is declared, so residual remains critical.

recommendations.action: Bind recipients to verified ticket identities and reject model-supplied destination changes at the mail MCP server.
Require raw human approval of recipient, subject, and body before every external send until recipient binding is deployed.
Alert on new recipient domains, unusual volume, and recipient-account mismatches; logging alone is insufficient.

findings.title: Unpinned MCP definitions and broad service credentials create a tool supply-chain path

attack_path.note: The agent accepts unpinned runtime definitions from the internal MCP servers.
Changed CRM tool behavior has access to all customer records.
Confidential CRM content enters the agent context.
The shared mail tool provides irreversible external egress.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric mechanically credits ctl.prompt_no_cross_customer because it covers cap.crm_read, but that prompt rule constrains cross-customer disclosure by the agent and does not constrain a compromised MCP server or poisoned tool definition. The supply-chain path therefore remains critical.

forecast.watch_signal: Changes in MCP tools/list output, TLS identity or endpoint configuration, authorization headers, or newly configured MCP servers.

evidence.observation: The configuration declares remote MCP endpoints and authorization headers but no tool-definition pinning, signed server identity, or change blocking.
The MCP services operate with full-CRM and any-recipient shared service credentials.
No preventive supply-chain control or tool approval gate is declared. The exact server deployment and authentication implementation are absent, limiting confidence to medium.

recommendations.action: Pin reviewed MCP tool definitions or hashes, verify server identity, and block execution when definitions or endpoints drift.
Replace broad static service credentials with short-lived, requester- and task-scoped authorization.

rating.rationale: Untrusted inbound email can directly reach an irreversible, any-recipient shared mail capability, so both inherent and residual risk are critical; SIEM logging is detective and the anger-based escalation rule is not a security gate. The CRM exfiltration path has critical inherent risk and high residual risk because its only preventive control is a dependent prompt rule. If the model is upgraded or task horizons grow, that rule fails and the path returns to critical. Unpinned MCP definitions combined with broad service credentials add a separate critical supply-chain path. Requester-scoped CRM authorization and recipient binding are the structural controls that most directly sever these paths.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in 01_support_triage.md, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, complete MCP tool manifests, runtime deployment configuration, network policy, authentication design, approval UI, model identity, evaluation results, or SIEM alert and review procedures were provided.
The CRM record input is rated unknown because the artifact does not identify which fields are customer-authored or whether tool output is treated purely as data.
The MCP supply-chain finding has medium confidence because server identity verification, transport enforcement, definition-change handling, and credential implementation are not described.
